content.title: Thunder vs. Magic: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/17/26)
content.text: The Oklahoma City Thunder (53–15) visit the Orlando Magic (38–29) tonight at the Kia Center in Orlando. The Thunder come into tonight’s matchup riding an eight-game winning streak. On Sunday, they defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 116–103 — their first double-digit win in five games. Chet Holmgren led with 21 points on 9-of-13 shooting, while Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Isaiah Joe followed with 20 points apiece. OKC shot just 42% from the field, but made up for it on defense, making 16 steals and scoring 29 points off 25 Minnesota turnovers. Orlando, meanwhile, saw its seven-game winning streak snapped by the Atlanta Hawks last night in a 124–112 defeat. Paolo Banchero and Desmond Bane cooled off, scoring just 18 points each and combining for 10-of-26 shooting. Banchero entered Monday’s matchup averaging 25.6 PPG in March, with Bane right behind him at 22.8 PPG. The Magic trailed by as many as 29 points and cut the deficit to 12, but their comeback stalled there. The Thunder haven’t been dominant for most of this win streak, with several wins coming by three points or less. But they excel at late-game stops and manufacturing points when it matters the most. Expect them to prevail in a tight finish. Prediction: Oklahoma City Thunder 118, Orlando Magic 113 Injury Report Oklahoma City Thunder Branden Carlson — Out (Back) Jalen Williams — Out (Hamstring) Thomas Sorber — OFS (Knee) Orlando Magic Anthony Black — Out (Abdomen) Franz Wagner — Out (Ankle) Jonathan Isaac — Out (Knee) How to Watch Thunder vs. Magic Tip-off for today’s Thunder-Magic game is set for 7:00 PM Eastern / 6:00 PM Central at the Kia Center in Orlando. The game airs live locally on FanDuel Sports Network Oklahoma and FanDuel Sports Network Florida. Fans in the OKC and Orlando broadcast markets without a FanDuel Sports Network subscription can purchase one on Amazon here. Out-of-market viewers can stream the matchup on NBA League Pass for free on Amazon Prime Video with a 7-day free trial here. Amazon also offers a discounted subscription that starts at $12.74 for the first two months (then $16.99/month). The subscription also includes access to NBA TV. Fans can also choose a Team Pass to follow one team’s games for $13.99 per month.
